CHANGES (list ALL modifications, one or multiple):

Change #1: [Category: Model Architecture]
- What: In model_design, add one trainable scalar bias per item, initialized to zero, to both positive and negative logits: score(u, i) = existing history-aware dot product + bias(i). Optimize these biases with the existing sampled-softmax objective and regularization coefficient; export them with the embeddings and update the predictor writer so validation and host inference use identical scoring.
- Why: Uniformly sampled evaluation candidates make an item's general likelihood of being selected useful alongside personalized compatibility. A separate bias lets the model learn this component without forcing embedding norms to represent both popularity and preference.

---

WHY current solution limited:
- Root cause: The current scorer represents every ranking signal through embedding dot products, while normalized graph propagation attenuates direct item-degree information; it has no explicit item intercept.
- Evidence: This limitation is visible in the scoring implementation. The graph model improves macro HR@10 from 0.505 to 0.5575 but reduces Electronics HR@10 from 0.420 to 0.365; these results motivate testing additional scoring flexibility, although they do not establish popularity calibration as the cause.

HOW these changes address it:
- Mechanism: Sampled softmax will learn item intercepts from training positives versus uniformly sampled unseen negatives, allowing embeddings to focus more on compatibility.
- Expected improvement: Predict a modest increase in macro validation HR@10 above 0.5575; treat this as an experimental hypothesis and compare all four category scores against the parent.
- Synergy: The bias complements the existing graph and recency-weighted representations without replacing either.

KEEP UNCHANGED (must explicitly list):
- Random seed: preprocessing seed=0; training and evaluation seed=42.
- Data split: identical supplied training and validation splits; no hidden test access or additional data.
- All four categories, dataset routing, DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and trial-local artifacts.
- Two-layer LightGCN, dimension 64, complete histories, recency half-life 10, profile coefficient 0.5, and target-excluded training profiles.
- Adam learning rate 0.003, 32 uniform training negatives, batch size 8192, eight steps per epoch, and SASREC_EPOCHS default 200.
- Existing checkpoint selection, early stopping, and single-GPU execution.
- Validation HR@10 with 200 users per category, 99 unique negatives, evaluation seed=42, and equal-weight category macro averaging; final predictions remain the host-generated output from working/predict.py.
